name: Steam cracking (naphtha, ethane, LPG)
principle: Hydrocarbon feed is diluted with steam and passed through coils in gas-fired furnaces at about 800 to 850 °C for a fraction of a second, which breaks it into ethylene, propylene and other olefins. The effluent is quenched to stop reactions, compressed, and separated by cryogenic distillation. Ethane gives mostly ethylene; naphtha gives a wider product slate including propylene, butadiene and aromatics.

limitations: One of the largest industrial CO2 sources (furnace fuel)
